subject: Intermittent WebSocket blackout during high-concurrency trial — exec sync requested
messages:
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@clearline.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: SRE Team <ops@clearline.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Live demo blackout during throughput spike — urgent

Hi Marissa,

We were running the stress/demo workload this morning (concurrent sessions ~420) and at 08:05 PST several of our clients hit silent streams: the WebSocket connections remain open but the token stream pauses for 6-18s intermittently, and then sometimes resumes with a big burst. This is causing our UI to show a frozen response and leads to repeated client retries.

We've attached logs and a pcap. Key observations from our side:
- Problem appears during high concurrency + long prefix prompts.
- Client-side shows normal keepalive heartbeats; server-side appears to push nothing for intervals.
- When it resumes, there's often a sequence of >200 tokens in one burst.

This is blocking our final acceptance tests today and we have a renewal discussion scheduled with our procurement team tomorrow. Can you escalate to engineering and let us know a mitigation (rollback, routing change, config) we can apply immediately?

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Platform
Clearline AI

Subject: RE: Live demo blackout during throughput spike — exec sync requested

Team — quick technical summary and action items after triage session:

What we observed
- Replayed pcap + logs show repeated long silent windows on the application path where the upstream inferred payload sender thread stalls in the proxy layer; keepalives are intact so TCP-level connection is fine.
- The stall correlates with requests that hit a particular serving host pool (pool-gamma-7) under high concurrent KV-cache pressure and long prefixes; the runtime serialized several emit operations that stacked up and then flushed as a large chunk.
- No error-rate spike on the model container itself; rather an ordering/coalescing issue in the proxy-to-runtime piping layer under burst pressure.

Immediate mitigations (next 90 minutes)
- Routing: move Clearline traffic to pool-gamma-3 (already done by infra) to spread load.
- Proxy tuning: enabled a mitigated emit flush window (reduce coalescing threshold) to prevent long silent windows; this is deployed to the edge in canary.
- Fallback: we can route Clearline to the non-proxy direct endpoint (Alex already flipped this) — rollback to previous proxy config is available if needed.

Longer-term work (tracked)
- Engineering ticket INF-3248: fix ordering edge-case in proxy-to-runtime backpressure path (owner: Jonas).
- Performance test: augment burst-sim tests to include long-prefix KV-cache pressure scenarios.

Executive ask
- Grace, can you join a 30 minute sync at 16:00 PST to prep a short customer-facing summary for procurement? We want to confirm whether Clearline keeps bypass for the next 24 hours and whether they require an SLA concession.
- Marissa, please escalate to VP Eng if we see >1.5 occurrences / 1,000 sessions over the next 2 hours — we should be ready to schedule an after-hours patch window.

I'll keep the canary monitor running and ping with rollback instructions if we see any regression from the tuning change.

—David
Senior SRE Manager, Redwood Inference
